strings.name: Usain Bolt
strings.summary: Bolt brought sprinting into global popular culture through 100m and 200m world records, eight Olympic golds and a distinctive public presence. He won both individual sprints at three consecutive Olympics and later promoted athletics. His medal total accounts for the withdrawn Beijing relay title.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones; competitions, affiliations and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive match log.
strings.influence.rationale: Sprint world records and Olympic titles converted track performance into worldwide popular influence.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Early training
strings.facts.fact-2.value: William Knibb Memorial High School; youth athletics
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Sprint world records
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Ran 9.58 seconds for 100m and 19.19 for 200m in 2009.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Sustained Olympic success
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won both individual sprints at three Olympics; his corrected Olympic gold total is eight.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Athletics promotion
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Appeared in Budapest as an ambassador for the World Athletics Ultimate Championship.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Retired from athletics
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Ended elite sprint competition after the London World Championships.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Beijing relay gold withdrawn
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Teammate Nesta Carter’s positive retest cost the team its 2008 gold; it was not Bolt’s positive test.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Three golds in Rio
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won 100m, 200m and 4×100m, completing his third Olympic individual sprint double.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Three more in London
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Again won both individual sprints and the relay.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Two world records
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Set the 9.58 and 19.19 records at the Berlin World Championships.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Beijing individual double
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won 100m and 200m in world-record times; the relay title was later withdrawn.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Olympic debut
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Contested the Athens 200m but did not reach the final.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: World junior champion
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won the 200m world junior title in Kingston, gaining international attention.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Jamaica
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Grew up in Trelawny and increasingly focused on sprinting during school.
